summaries.summary: Curriculum and instruction is the field of education research concerned with what is taught and how it is taught: the design, organization, and content of curricula and the didactic methods by which they are delivered. Within the American Educational Research Association the field is institutionalized as Division B, "Curriculum Studies," and Division C, "Learning & Instruction," two of the association's standing research divisions. In the Universal Decimal Classification its instructional dimension is grouped under UDC 37.02, captioned "General questions of didactics and method," within the education class (UDC 37). The field examines curriculum aims, subject matter, instructional design, and methods of teaching across the elementary, secondary, and tertiary levels.

summaries.summary: Educational policy is the field of education research that studies the formation, content, and effects of the policies and political processes governing education systems. Within the American Educational Research Association it is institutionalized as Division L, "Educational Policy & Politics," one of the association's standing research divisions. In the Universal Decimal Classification the policy and theory of education are grouped under UDC 37.01, captioned "Fundamentals of education. Theory, policy, etc.," within the education class (UDC 37). The field analyzes how educational policy is made and implemented and how it shapes practice across levels of schooling.

summaries.summary: Higher education, as a field of study, is the scholarly inquiry into postsecondary (tertiary) education: its institutions, organization, policy, and outcomes. The Association for the Study of Higher Education (ASHE) describes itself as "a vibrant scholarly community ... dedicated to advancing the study of higher education," with the stated purpose "To foster scholarly inquiry for the purpose of increasing knowledge about and the understanding of higher education to enhance policy and practice." Within the American Educational Research Association the field is institutionalized as Division J, "Postsecondary Education," which the association states "focuses on scholars, professionals, and students who study postsecondary issues such as higher education organizations, policy, college student experiences and transitions, and university curricular issues." Its object of study is grouped in the Universal Decimal Classification under UDC 378, "Higher education. Universities. Academic study."

summaries.summary: Special education is the field concerned with the education of children whose needs differ from the typical to a degree requiring adapted instruction. Encyclopaedia Britannica defines it as "the education of children who differ socially, mentally, or physically from the average to such an extent that they require modifications of usual school practices," serving "children with emotional, behavioral, or cognitive impairments or with intellectual, hearing, vision, speech, or learning disabilities; gifted children with advanced academic abilities; and children with orthopedic or neurological impairments." The principal learned body in the field, the Council for Exceptional Children (CEC), describes itself as a "professional organization dedicated to improving the success of children and youth with disabilities and/or gifts and talents." In the Universal Decimal Classification the field is grouped under UDC 376, "Education, teaching, training of special groups of persons. Special schools."

summaries.summary: Constitutional law is the branch of law governing the basic structure and powers of the state and the fundamental rights of individuals within it. Encyclopaedia Britannica defines it as "the body of rules, doctrines, and practices that govern the operation of political communities," noting that "Modern constitutional law is the offspring of nationalism as well as of the idea that the state must protect certain fundamental rights of the individual." Britannica adds that "A political community's constitution articulates the principles determining the institutions to which the task of governing is entrusted, along with their respective powers." In the Universal Decimal Classification the field falls under UDC 342, captioned "Public law. Constitutional law. Administrative law," within the law class (UDC 34, "Law. Jurisprudence").

summaries.summary: International law is the branch of law governing relations between states and other entities recognized as actors on the international plane. Encyclopaedia Britannica defines it as "the body of legal rules, norms, and standards that apply between sovereign states and other entities that are legally recognized as international actors," noting that "The term was coined by the English philosopher Jeremy Bentham." The American Society of International Law (ASIL) states that its mission "is to foster the study of international law and to promote the establishment and maintenance of international relations on the basis of law and justice," describing itself as an organization "founded in 1906 and chartered by Congress in 1950." In the Universal Decimal Classification the field falls under UDC 341, "International law," within the law class (UDC 34, "Law. Jurisprudence").

summaries.summary: Criminal law is the branch of law concerned with offenses against the public and the punishment of those who commit them. Encyclopaedia Britannica defines it as "the body of law that defines criminal offenses, regulates the apprehension, charging, and trial of suspected persons, and fixes penalties and modes of treatment applicable to convicted offenders." Britannica situates it as "only one of the devices by which organized societies protect the security of individual interests and ensure the survival of the group," and notes that the line between criminal law and tort law "is difficult to draw with real precision." In the Universal Decimal Classification the field falls under UDC 343, "Criminal law. Penal offences," within the law class (UDC 34, "Law. Jurisprudence").

summaries.summary: Civil law, in the branch-of-law sense, is the body of law governing non-criminal legal relationships between persons — the law of contracts, property, torts, family, and obligations — as distinct from criminal law and from public law. Encyclopaedia Britannica characterizes private law, the broader category to which this branch belongs, as "private law regulating the actions, interests, and obligations of private persons." In the Universal Decimal Classification the branch is grouped under UDC 347, captioned "Civil law," which sits alongside UDC 341 "International law," UDC 342 "Public law. Constitutional law. Administrative law," and UDC 343 "Criminal law. Penal offences" within the law class (UDC 34, "Law. Jurisprudence"). This referent is the substantive branch of private law, not a national or continental legal system.

Used as a characterization of the private-law category, not as a full standalone definition of the civil-law branch — the branch's distinct placement is carried by UDC 347.

The enumeration of contracts, property, torts, family, and obligations as the branch's subject matter is the conventional scope of the branch but is asserted here without a single fetched source enumerating all of them verbatim; QC should confirm against a gate-grade source or trim the enumeration. The UDC 347 caption confirms only the label 'Civil law' and its placement within the law class.
